note: On profile he is the ICP's own worked example — the stated definition names physicians explicitly, and he is a practising dentist with plans to open his own practice. Health is unambiguously the neglected area: eight months to a year of drift while a move, a new job, a depressive episode and digestive illness took the foreground. He is also nowhere near the excluded profile, at 169 lb and 5'8" with a full kettlebell set and a daily gym habit. He misses on income and on starting point. Income fails the affordability test rather than the earnings one — dental school debt, an $8,000 relocation fund and a savings programme toward the $80,000-$100,000 a lender requires mean the money exists on paper and not in practice: 'my income is enough to pay for my school loans, and then pay for my rent, and then a few things here and there.' And he is not good-to-great — the rep's own reflect-back was 'basically you're fighting for your life', which the prospect accepted. He is the second case in this batch of a prospect who is exactly who the ICP describes and still cannot buy, which suggests the binding constraint is liquidity rather than income.
